title: Annotatio I §.IV close IMPLICITE Lutheran: Replies (3)–(5) — part/whole, demonstration, Carlstadt; stop before §.V
pass_a_gloss: (3.) The Complex being put, not conceded, a part is thus predicated of the whole, and the proposition becomes tropical. (4.) Demonstration does not remove the complex, therefore neither the trope. (5.) Demonstration pertains only to that which could be demonstrated to the senses; and this was either Christ’s body sitting at the table — thus a Carlstadian proposition would arise — or the bread which Christ was carrying in His hands — thus our metonymy of sign for thing signified would obtain — or finally another invisible body of Christ: but this first could not be demonstrated to sense, because by hypothesis it is invisible; then it introduces two bodies of Christ, one visible, one invisible — besides that thirdly either body received together with the bread makes both the Complex (not yet proved, nay disapproved by Luther) and propriety (assaulted with great effort and hardly to be conceded) return.
pass_b_english: (3.) Grant the Complex only for argument: then a part is predicated of the whole, and the proposition is tropical.
(4.) A demonstrative does not cancel the complex — therefore not the trope either.

(5.) Sense can only point to what senses reach: the sitting body (Carlstadt), the bread in Christ’s hands (Reformed sign-for-signified metonymy), or an invisible second body — which cannot be shown to sense, doubles Christ’s bodies, and drags back both the unproved Complex Luther rejected and a propriety hardly to be conceded.
source_text: (3.) Positô, non concessô Complexô, partem sic praedicari de toto, & propositionem tropicam fieri. (4.) Demonstrationem non tollere complexum, Ergo nec tropum. (5.) Demonstrationem tantum ad illud pertinere, quod demonstrari sensibus poterat; & hoc vel erat corpus Christi, mensae assidens: sic verò propositionem enasci Carlstadianam, vel panis, quem in manibus gestabat Christus: sic verò nostram obtenturam metonymiam signi pro signato; vel denique aliud invisibile corpus Christi: sed hoc primò non poterat sensui demonstrari, quia ex hypothesi invisibile est; dein duo corpora Christi inducit, aliud visibile, aliud invisibile, praeterquàm quòd tertiò alterutrum corpus unà cum pane acceptum, tam Complexum, nondum probatum, quin Luthero improbatum, quàm proprietatem, magno molimine impugnatam, aegreque concedendam, reducem facit.

choices.english: metonymy of sign for thing signified

notes: Replies (3)–(5); Carlstadt vs metonymy; stop before §.V.
